midnat.explanation: "Midnat" means "midnight", twelve o'clock at night. Do not mix it up with "middag" (noon or dinner): "Vi spiser middag klokken seks" (We eat dinner at six).

sentence.da: Festen slutter først ved **midnat**.
sentence.en: The party only ends at midnight.

midt.explanation: "Midt" means "in the middle". It usually comes with "i" (in) or "på" (on): "midt i byen" (in the middle of town), "midt på dagen" (in the middle of the day).

forms.en: in the middle of the room
in the middle of the night

sentence.da: Der står et træ **midt** i haven.
sentence.en: There is a tree in the middle of the garden.

mig.explanation: "Mig" means "me": "Han ser mig" (He sees me). Do not mix it up with "jeg" (I): "Jeg ser ham" (I see him). "Mig" is also the form after "til" (to) and "med" (with): "til mig" (to me), "med mig" (with me). With some verbs it means "myself": "Jeg vasker mig" (I wash myself).

sentence.da: Min ven giver **mig** en gave.
sentence.en: My friend gives me a gift.

mild.explanation: "Mild" means "mild", not sharp or extreme. It works for weather and for food: "Vinteren er mild i år" (The winter is mild this year), "en mild ost" (a mild cheese).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have en **mild** sauce uden chili.
sentence.en: I want a mild sauce without chili.

militær.explanation: "Militær" means "military", about the armed forces. The same word is used for the armed forces themselves: "Han er i militæret" (He is in the military).

sentence.da: Soldaterne træner på en **militær** base uden for byen.
sentence.en: The soldiers train at a military base outside the town.

million.explanation: "En million" means "a million". With more than one, it becomes "millioner": "to millioner mennesker" (two million people). Do not mix it up with "en milliard" (a billion, which is 1,000 million).

sentence.da: Han vandt en **million** kroner i lotteriet.
sentence.en: He won a million kroner in the lottery.

min.explanation: "Min" means "my" or "mine" and is used with en-words. For et-words, use "mit" (my), as in "mit hus" (my house), and for several things use "mine", as in "mine børn" (my children).

sentence.da: Jeg har en bil. **Min** bil er rød.
sentence.en: I have a car. My car is red.

mindre.explanation: "Mindre" means both "less" (an amount) and "smaller" (a size): "mindre kaffe" (less coffee), "et mindre hus" (a smaller house).

sentence.da: Et lille hus er **mindre** end et stort.
sentence.en: A small house is smaller than a big one.

mindst.explanation: "Mindst" means "least" and also "at least": "Hvem har mindst tid?" (Who has the least time?) With a number it sets the lowest amount: "mindst fem" (at least five).

forms.en: I will wait at least an hour

sentence.da: Du skal sove **mindst** otte timer.
sentence.en: You should sleep at least eight hours.

mine.explanation: "Mine" means "my" or "mine" when there is more than one thing: "mine bøger" (my books), "mine huse" (my houses). With one thing, Danes use "min" for en-words, as in "min bog" (my book), and "mit" for et-words, as in "mit hus" (my house). "Mine" also works alone: "Bøgerne er mine" (The books are mine).

sentence.da: **Mine** børn hedder Peter og Anna.
sentence.en: My children are called Peter and Anna.

minigolf.explanation: "Minigolf" means "mini golf", the small golf game with fun obstacles.

sentence.da: I **minigolf** slår man bolden gennem en lille tunnel.
sentence.en: In mini golf, you hit the ball through a small tunnel.

minimal.explanation: "Minimal" means "minimal", the smallest amount possible or needed.

sentence.da: Risikoen for fejl er **minimal**, fordi alt bliver tjekket to gange.
sentence.en: The risk of errors is minimal because everything is checked twice.

misfornøjet.explanation: "Misfornøjet" means "dissatisfied", unhappy because something is not as you hoped. The start mis- gives the idea of something wrong or bad, as in "at misforstå" (to misunderstand).

sentence.da: Kunden var **misfornøjet**, fordi maden kom for sent.
sentence.en: The customer was dissatisfied because the food came too late.

misforstået.explanation: "Misforstået" means "misunderstood", for a person or an idea that others do not see correctly: "et misforstået geni" (a misunderstood genius). It can also mean "misguided": "misforstået loyalitet" (misguided loyalty).

sentence.da: Hendes joke blev **misforstået**, så hun forklarede den igen.
sentence.en: Her joke was misunderstood, so she explained it again.

misinformation.explanation: "Misinformation" means "misinformation", false information that is passed on, often by people who believe it is true.

sentence.da: **Misinformation** spredes hurtigt på sociale medier, selv når folk mener det godt.
sentence.en: Misinformation spreads quickly on social media, even when people mean well.

mistillid.explanation: "En mistillid" means "distrust", the feeling that someone cannot be trusted. It is the opposite of "tillid" (trust). In politics, "et mistillidsvotum" (a vote of no confidence) is a vote against a government.

sentence.da: Der er stor **mistillid** mellem de to lande efter krigen.
sentence.en: There is great distrust between the two countries after the war.

mistænkelig.explanation: "Mistænkelig" means "suspicious", for something that looks wrong and makes others distrust it: "en mistænkelig lyd" (a suspicious sound). A person who feels distrust toward others is "mistænksom" (distrustful), a different word.

sentence.da: Manden virkede **mistænkelig**, fordi han skjulte sit ansigt.
sentence.en: The man seemed suspicious because he hid his face.

mistænksom.explanation: "Mistænksom" means "suspicious", for a person who does not trust others easily: "en mistænksom nabo" (a suspicious neighbor). Something that looks wrong is "mistænkelig" (suspicious-looking), a different word.

sentence.da: Hunden er **mistænksom** over for fremmede, og den gøer højt.
sentence.en: The dog is suspicious of strangers, and it barks loudly.

mistænkt.explanation: "Mistænkt" means "suspected", for a person the police think may have committed a crime. The noun "en mistænkt" means "a suspect": "Politiet har en mistænkt" (The police have a suspect).

sentence.da: Manden er **mistænkt** for tyveriet, men han nægter.
sentence.en: The man is suspected of the theft, but he denies it.

misundelig.explanation: "Misundelig" means "envious", wanting what someone else has. To say of whom, add "på" (of): "Han er misundelig på sin kollega" (He is envious of his coworker).

sentence.da: Jeg er **misundelig** på din nye bil.
sentence.en: I am envious of your new car.

misundelse.explanation: "En misundelse" means "envy", the unhappy feeling when someone else has something you want. The word for fear of losing someone's love to another person is "jalousi" (jealousy).

sentence.da: Hun følte **misundelse**, da veninden fik et drømmejob.
sentence.en: She felt envy when her friend got a dream job.

misvisende.explanation: "Misvisende" means "misleading", giving a false picture of something.

sentence.da: Overskriften er **misvisende**, fordi artiklen siger noget andet.
sentence.en: The headline is misleading because the article says something else.

mit.explanation: "Mit" means "my" or "mine" and goes with et-words, such as "et hus" (a house). En-words take "min" (my): "min bil" (my car). With more than one thing, use "mine" (my): "mine huse" (my houses).

sentence.da: Jeg har et hus. **Mit** hus er gult.
sentence.en: I have a house. My house is yellow.

mod.explanation: "Mod" means "toward" and also "against". For a direction: "Han går mod døren" (He walks toward the door). For an opponent: "Vi spiller mod Sverige" (We play against Sweden). To say you are against an idea, use "imod" (against): "Jeg er imod det" (I am against it).

sentence.da: Vi går **mod** stationen.
sentence.en: We are walking toward the station.

mode.explanation: "Mode" means "fashion", the clothes and styles people like now. Do not mix it up with "en måde" (a way): "en god måde" (a good way).

sentence.da: Min søster elsker **mode** og køber meget tøj.
sentence.en: My sister loves fashion and buys a lot of clothes.

moderigtig.explanation: "Moderigtig" means "fashionable", in line with what is in style right now. It is built from mode (fashion) and rigtig (right), so it is literally "right for the fashion".

sentence.da: Jakken er **moderigtig** nu, men måske ikke næste år.
sentence.en: The jacket is fashionable now, but maybe not next year.

moderne.explanation: "Moderne" means "modern", for things that are up to date, such as styles and art. The opposite is "gammeldags" (old-fashioned).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et **moderne** hus med store vinduer.
sentence.en: We live in a modern house with big windows.

modgang.explanation: "En modgang" means "adversity", a period when things go badly and life is hard. It is the opposite of "medgang" (good fortune), and the two appear together in "i medgang og modgang" (in good times and bad).

sentence.da: Gode venner står ved din side, når du har **modgang**.
sentence.en: Good friends stand by your side when you face adversity.

modig.explanation: "Modig" means "brave" and describes someone who is not afraid of hard or scary things. The opposite is "bange" (scared).

sentence.da: Hun er **modig** og tør tale foran hundrede mennesker.
sentence.en: She is brave and dares to speak in front of a hundred people.

modløs.explanation: "Modløs" means "discouraged", having lost heart and the will to keep trying. It is built from mod (courage) and -løs (without), so it is literally without courage.

sentence.da: Efter det dårlige resultat blev hun **modløs** og ville give op.
sentence.en: After the bad result she became discouraged and wanted to give up.

modsat.explanation: "Modsat" means "opposite", the other way around. To name the opposite itself, say "det modsatte": "Det modsatte af varm er kold" (The opposite of hot is cold).

sentence.da: Han gik til højre, og jeg gik i **modsat** retning.
sentence.en: He went right, and I went in the opposite direction.

modstandsdygtig.explanation: "Modstandsdygtig" means "resilient", able to hold up against harm such as illness, cold or stress: "en modstandsdygtig plante" (a resilient plant). It is built from modstand (resistance) and dygtig (skilled).

sentence.da: Planten er **modstandsdygtig** og klarer sig godt i frost.
sentence.en: The plant is resilient and does well in frost.

moms.explanation: "Moms" means "VAT" or "sales tax", the tax that is added to prices in shops. To ask about it, say: "Er det med moms?" (Is VAT included?)

sentence.da: Prisen er tusind kroner med **moms**.
sentence.en: The price is a thousand kroner with VAT.

moralsk.explanation: "Moralsk" means "moral", for what people feel is right and wrong, not for what the law says: "et moralsk valg" (a moral choice).

sentence.da: Er det forkert at lyve? Det er et **moralsk** spørgsmål.
sentence.en: Is it wrong to lie? That is a moral question.

morgenmad.explanation: "Morgenmad" means "breakfast". It is morgen (morning) and mad (food) joined together. This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Jeg spiser morgenmad" (I eat breakfast).

sentence.da: Om morgenen spiser jeg **morgenmad**: brød og kaffe.
sentence.en: In the morning I eat breakfast: bread and coffee.

morsom.explanation: "Morsom" means "funny" in a light, amusing way. In everyday speech, many people say "sjov" (fun) instead: "en sjov fyr" (a fun guy).

sentence.da: Han er **morsom** og får alle til at le.
sentence.en: He is funny and makes everyone laugh.

mos.explanation: "Et mos" means both "moss", the soft green plant that grows on stones and trees, and "mash", food mashed soft. You can tell from the context of the sentence whether it means "moss" or "mash".

sentence.da: Der vokser **mos** på de gamle sten.
sentence.en: Moss grows on the old stones.

motion.explanation: "Motion" means "exercise", physical activity that is good for you. For a single exercise in a lesson, use "en øvelse" (an exercise): "en øvelse i grammatik" (a grammar exercise).

sentence.da: Jeg går en lang tur for at få **motion**.
sentence.en: I take a long walk to get exercise.

motivation.explanation: "Motivation" means "motivation", the drive that makes you want to do something.

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen **motivation** til at træne.
sentence.en: I have no motivation to exercise.

mozzarella.explanation: "Mozzarella" means "mozzarella", a soft, mild Italian cheese that melts well.

sentence.da: Til salaten køber jeg frisk **mozzarella** og tomater.
sentence.en: For the salad, I buy fresh mozzarella and tomatoes.

mudder.explanation: "Et mudder" means "mud", wet, soft earth that sticks to your shoes and sinks under your feet.

sentence.da: Efter regnen var marken fuld af **mudder**.
sentence.en: After the rain the field was full of mud.

mulig.explanation: "Mulig" means "possible". It is used in the set phrase "så hurtigt som muligt" (as fast as possible).

sentence.da: Regn er **mulig** i morgen, men ikke sikker.
sentence.en: Rain is possible tomorrow, but not certain.

muligvis.explanation: "Muligvis" means "possibly" and is built from mulig (possible). It can stand alone as an answer: "Kommer hun? Muligvis." (Is she coming? Possibly.)

sentence.da: Vi tager **muligvis** til Spanien i sommer.
sentence.en: We are possibly going to Spain this summer.

mundtlig.explanation: "Mundtlig" means "oral" or "spoken", done by speaking and not by writing: "en mundtlig eksamen" (an oral exam). It comes from en mund (a mouth), so it is literally "of the mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg skal ikke skrive, fordi eksamen er **mundtlig**.
sentence.en: I do not have to write because the exam is oral.

munter.explanation: "Munter" means "cheerful", in a bright mood full of energy.

sentence.da: Hun var **munter** og sang hele vejen hjem.
sentence.en: She was cheerful and sang all the way home.

musik.explanation: "Musik" means "music". This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Jeg elsker musik" (I love music). For a school lesson, "Jeg har musik" means "I have music class".

sentence.da: Jeg lytter gerne til **musik**.
sentence.en: I like listening to music.

musikalsk.explanation: "Musikalsk" means "musical", for a person who is good at music or loves it. It can describe a whole group of people too: "en musikalsk familie" (a musical family).

sentence.da: Min datter er meget **musikalsk** og elsker at synge.
sentence.en: My daughter is very musical and loves to sing.

muskuløs.explanation: "Muskuløs" means "muscular", with big muscles you can see. A person can be "stærk" (strong) without being muskuløs: "Han er stærk, men ikke muskuløs" (He is strong, but not muscular).

sentence.da: Gymnasten er **muskuløs**, fordi han træner hver dag.
sentence.en: The gymnast is muscular because he trains every day.

muslimsk.explanation: "Muslimsk" means "Muslim" and describes things linked to that faith. A person is "en muslim" (a Muslim), while "muslimsk" goes with things: "muslimske skikke" (Muslim customs), "en muslimsk bøn" (a Muslim prayer).

sentence.da: Ramadanen er en **muslimsk** tradition.
sentence.en: Ramadan is a Muslim tradition.

mystisk.explanation: "Mystisk" means "mysterious", for something you cannot explain: "en mystisk lyd om natten" (a mysterious sound at night). For something that is only odd, say "mærkelig" (strange): "en mærkelig hat" (a strange hat).

sentence.da: Der står en **mystisk** mand uden for vores dør.
sentence.en: A mysterious man is standing outside our door.

mytologi.explanation: "En mytologi" means "mythology", the old stories about gods and heroes that a people once believed in.

sentence.da: Thor er en figur i den nordiske **mytologi**.
sentence.en: Thor is a figure in Norse mythology.

må jeg bede om regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg bede om regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" and is a polite way to ask for it at a restaurant. The same start works for other requests: "Må jeg bede om et glas vand?" (May I have a glass of water?).

sentence.da: Vi har spist. **Må jeg bede om regningen?**
sentence.en: We have eaten. May I have the bill?

må jeg få regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg få regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" The same start works for other requests: "Må jeg få en kop kaffe?" (May I have a cup of coffee?).

forms.da: Må jeg få en kop kaffe?
forms.en: May I have a cup of coffee?

related.en: may I have the bill? (more formal)

sentence.da: Maden var god. **Må jeg få regningen?**
sentence.en: The food was good. May I have the bill?

målrettet.explanation: "Målrettet" means "goal-oriented", working steadily toward a clear goal without getting distracted: "en målrettet indsats" (a focused effort). It is built from et mål (a goal) and rettet (aimed).

sentence.da: Hun er **målrettet** og ved præcis, hvad hun vil.
sentence.en: She is goal-oriented and knows exactly what she wants.

månedsvis.explanation: "Månedsvis" means "for months" and says something went on month after month: "Vi har ventet månedsvis" (We have waited for months). It is built from en måned (a month) and the ending -vis.

sentence.da: Vi ventede **månedsvis** på svar fra kommunen.
sentence.en: We waited for months for an answer from the municipality.

måske.explanation: "Måske" means "maybe" or "perhaps". It can be a whole answer: "Kommer du? Måske." (Are you coming? Maybe.)

sentence.da: **Måske** kommer han i morgen.
sentence.en: Maybe he will come tomorrow.

mægtig.explanation: "Mægtig" means "mighty" or "powerful", for anything with great strength or size that impresses, such as rulers, nations and large animals: "et mægtigt træ" (a mighty tree). In everyday speech, it can also mean "really" before another word: "mægtig flot" (really nice).

sentence.da: Ørnen er en **mægtig** fugl med store vinger.
sentence.en: The eagle is a mighty bird with large wings.

mælk.explanation: "Mælk" means "milk". To count it, use a measure: "en liter mælk" (a liter of milk).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **mælk** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of milk every morning.

mærkbar.explanation: "Mærkbar" means "noticeable", big enough that you can feel or see it: "en mærkbar forskel" (a noticeable difference). It is built from at mærke (to notice) and -bar (able to be).

sentence.da: Forskellen er **mærkbar**, og alle kan se den.
sentence.en: The difference is noticeable and everyone can see it.

mærkelig.explanation: "Mærkelig" means "strange", something odd that stands out: "en mærkelig lugt" (a strange smell). It is built from at mærke (to notice), and "et mærke" (a brand, a mark) is from the same family: "et dyrt mærke" (an expensive brand).

sentence.da: Der er en **mærkelig** lyd i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a strange sound in the kitchen.

mæt.explanation: "Mæt" means "full" after eating: "Jeg er mæt" (I am full) is a polite way to turn down more food. After a meal, do not say "Jeg er fuld", which means "I am drunk".

sentence.da: Jeg har spist meget og er **mæt**.
sentence.en: I have eaten a lot and am full.

mættende.explanation: "Mættende" means "filling", said about food that keeps you from getting hungry again soon.

sentence.da: Havregrød er **mættende**, og man bliver ikke hurtigt sulten.
sentence.en: Oatmeal is filling and you do not get hungry quickly.

møbleret.explanation: "Møbleret" means "furnished", for a room or apartment that comes with furniture. Without furniture, say "umøbleret" (unfurnished).

sentence.da: Værelset er **møbleret** med seng, bord og stol.
sentence.en: The room is furnished with a bed, table and chair.

mør.explanation: "Mør" means "tender", for meat or other food that is soft and easy to cut or chew. The opposite is "sej" (tough): "Kødet er sejt" (The meat is tough).

sentence.da: Kødet er **mør**, fordi det har stået længe i ovnen.
sentence.en: The meat is tender because it has been in the oven a long time.

mørk.explanation: "Mørk" means "dark", for places with little light and for deep colors. It also goes in front of a color to make it deeper: "mørkeblå" (dark blue).

sentence.da: Om natten er himlen **mørk**.
sentence.en: At night the sky is dark.

mørke.explanation: "Mørke" means "darkness", the lack of light. To describe something dark, use "mørk" (dark): "et mørkt rum" (a dark room).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i **mørke**, når strømmen går.
sentence.en: We sit in the dark when the power goes out.

mørkeblå.explanation: "Mørkeblå" means "dark blue" or "navy". It is built from mørk (dark) and blå (blue). A bright blue like a clear sky is "himmelblå" (sky blue).

sentence.da: Himlen er **mørkeblå** før solopgang.
sentence.en: The sky is dark blue before sunrise.

mørkegrøn.explanation: "Mørkegrøn" means "dark green". It is built from mørk (dark) and grøn (green). A fresh green like grass is "græsgrøn" (grass green).

sentence.da: Granen er **mørkegrøn** hele året.
sentence.en: The fir tree is dark green all year.

mørketid.explanation: "En mørketid" means "a dark season", the time of year with very short days and little daylight.

sentence.da: I årets **mørketid** er dagene meget korte.
sentence.en: In the dark season of the year the days are very short.

mørkhåret.explanation: "Mørkhåret" means "dark-haired", with dark hair, usually brown or black. It is built from mørk (dark), hår (hair) and the ending -et. The same pattern gives "blåøjet" (blue-eyed).

sentence.da: Han er høj og **mørkhåret**, og han har blå øjne.
sentence.en: He is tall and dark-haired, and he has blue eyes.

müsli.explanation: "Müsli" means "muesli", the breakfast mix of grains, nuts and dried fruit.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **müsli** med mælk i en skål.
sentence.en: I eat muesli with milk in a bowl.

at narre.explanation: "At narre" means "to fool / trick", to make someone believe something that is not true, often for fun or in a small way. It is milder than "at snyde" (to cheat): "at narre sine venner" (to fool your friends).

sentence.da: Han forsøgte at **narre** mig med et falsk navn.
sentence.en: He tried to fool me with a fake name.

at navngive.explanation: "At navngive" means "to name", to give something an official name, such as a child, a ship or a new discovery. In daily talk Danes more often say "at kalde" (to call).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **navngive** den nye art efter hende.
sentence.en: The researchers want to name the new species after her.

at nedbryde.explanation: "At nedbryde" means "to break down" into smaller parts through a natural process: "Bakterier nedbryder affald" (Bacteria break down waste). It is also used for ideas: "nedbryde fordomme" (break down prejudices).

sentence.da: Svampe hjælper med at **nedbryde** døde blade i skoven.
sentence.en: Fungi help break down dead leaves in the forest.

at nedkæmpe.explanation: "At nedkæmpe" means "to defeat" or "to suppress", used when you act against something until it is under control or gone: "nedkæmpe et oprør" (put down a rebellion), "nedkæmpe en sygdom" (stamp out a disease).

sentence.da: Politiet skal **nedkæmpe** den voksende kriminalitet i området.
sentence.en: The police must bring the growing crime in the area under control.

at nedlægge.explanation: "At nedlægge" means "to shut down" something for good, such as a shop, a factory or a bus line: "nedlægge en buslinje" (shut down a bus line). Unlike "at lukke" (to close), which may be just for the night, it is permanent. It is also used for laying something down: "nedlægge en krans" (lay a wreath).

forms.en: I have shut down / laid down

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **nedlægge** den lille skole, fordi der er for få børn.
sentence.en: The city will shut down the small school because there are too few children.

at nedsætte.explanation: "At nedsætte" means "to reduce": to cut something down, such as a number, a speed or a level: "nedsætte farten" (reduce speed). It has a second meaning, to set up a group: "nedsætte en arbejdsgruppe" (set up a working group).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **nedsætte** priserne på alle jakker.
sentence.en: The store will reduce the prices on all jackets.

at nedtone.explanation: "At nedtone" means "to downplay": to make something sound less important or serious than it is: "Chefen nedtonede problemet" (The boss downplayed the problem). It is built from ned (down) and tone (tone), like turning the volume down.

sentence.da: Man bør ikke **nedtone** faren, når børn leger ved vandet.
sentence.en: You should not downplay the danger when children play by the water.

at nikke.explanation: "At nikke" means "to nod", to move your head down and up, usually to say yes. The opposite is "at ryste på hovedet" (to shake your head).

sentence.da: Hun begyndte at **nikke**, da han forklarede planen.
sentence.en: She began to nod when he explained the plan.

at nippe.explanation: "At nippe" means "to sip": to take small amounts of a drink slowly, for pleasure. Danish adds "til" (to): "nippe til teen" (sip the tea).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **nippe** til vinen, for jeg skal køre.
sentence.en: I will just sip the wine because I have to drive.

at notere.explanation: "At notere" means "to note down": you write something short so you remember it.

sentence.da: Kan du **notere** mit telefonnummer?
sentence.en: Can you note down my phone number?

at nusse.explanation: "At nusse" means "to cuddle / stroke", to touch an animal or a small child gently and lovingly, such as a cat or a dog.

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **nusse** den lille hvalp.
sentence.en: The children would like to cuddle the little puppy.

at nyde.explanation: "At nyde" means "to enjoy", slowly and on purpose. You say it when you take your time with something good: "Vi nyder middagen" (We are enjoying the dinner), "Jeg nyder min pause" (I am enjoying my break).

sentence.da: Vi vil **nyde** solen i parken i dag.
sentence.en: We want to enjoy the sun in the park today.

sentence.da: Jeg er forkølet og må **nyse** hele tiden.
sentence.en: I have a cold and have to sneeze all the time.

at nytte.explanation: "At nytte" means "to be of use", to have an effect or make a difference. It is mostly used when something does not work: "Det nytter ikke" (It is no use).

sentence.da: Det vil ikke **nytte** at råbe til ham.
sentence.en: It will not help to shout at him.

at nå.explanation: "At nå" means "to reach", and also "to make it" in time: "Jeg nåede det ikke" (I did not make it). For getting somewhere: "Vi nåede hjem" (We got home).

sentence.da: Jeg må løbe for at **nå** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to run to catch the bus.

at nå det.explanation: "At nå det" means "to make it", meaning to be in time: "Tror du, vi når det?" (Do you think we will make it?) With a thing, drop "det" (it): "Jeg nåede bussen" (I caught the bus).

sentence.da: Toget går om fem minutter, men vi kan **nå det**.
sentence.en: The train leaves in five minutes, but we can make it.

at nå toget.explanation: "At nå toget" means "to catch the train", arriving in time for it. Add "ikke" (not) if you are too late: "Jeg nåede ikke toget" (I missed the train).

sentence.da: Vi skal løbe for at **nå toget**.
sentence.en: We have to run to catch the train.

at nægte.explanation: "At nægte" means "to refuse": "Han nægter at komme" (He refuses to come). It also means "to deny": "Hun nægter, at hun tog den" (She denies that she took it).

sentence.da: Du kan **nægte** at svare.
sentence.en: You can refuse to answer.

at nærme sig.explanation: "At nærme sig" means "to approach", and "sig" changes with the person: "Vi nærmer os byen" (We are approaching the city). It works for time too: "Julen nærmer sig" (Christmas is getting closer).

sentence.da: Katten vil **nærme sig** fuglen langsomt.
sentence.en: The cat will approach the bird slowly.

at nævne.explanation: "At nævne" means "to mention", saying something briefly in passing: "Hun nævnte det ikke" (She did not mention it).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nævne** det for ham.
sentence.en: You must not mention it to him.

at nøjes med.explanation: "At nøjes med" means "to make do with", to accept less than you wanted and be fine with it: "Vi nøjes med en lille bil" (We make do with a small car).

sentence.da: Vi må **nøjes med** én kop kaffe i dag.
sentence.en: We must make do with one cup of coffee today.

at nøle.explanation: "At nøle" means "to hesitate", to wait a moment because you are unsure. Add "med at" (with to) before the action word: "Han nølede med at svare" (He hesitated to answer).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nøle**, hvis du har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not hesitate if you need help.

en nabo.explanation: "En nabo" means "a neighbor". The word is the same for a man and a woman: "Min nabo er en sød dame" (My neighbor is a nice lady).

sentence.da: Min **nabo** bor ved siden af.
sentence.en: My neighbor lives next door.

en nakke.explanation: "En nakke" means "the back of the neck" (the nape). The front of the neck is "en hals" (a neck or throat).

sentence.da: Jeg har en stiv **nakke** efter en lang bilkørsel.
sentence.en: I have a stiff neck after a long drive.

en narkoman.explanation: "En narkoman" means "a drug addict", a person who is addicted to drugs. It can sound harsh, so in care work you more often hear "en misbruger" (a person with a substance problem).

sentence.da: En **narkoman** er afhængig af stoffer og har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: A drug addict is dependent on drugs and needs help.

en nat.explanation: "En nat" means "a night", the dark time when most people sleep. Common phrases are "i nat" (tonight or last night), "om natten" (at night) and "godnat" (good night).

sentence.da: En **nat** varer fra aften til morgen.
sentence.en: A night lasts from evening to morning.

en nation.explanation: "En nation" means "a nation", a country seen as one people. It is also in the name "De Forenede Nationer" (the United Nations).

sentence.da: Danmark er en lille **nation** i Europa.
sentence.en: Denmark is a small nation in Europe.

en nationalbank.explanation: "En nationalbank" means "a central bank", the main bank of a country, a bank for the other banks and the state. It is not for ordinary customers: you do not have an account there.

sentence.da: Landets **nationalbank** bestemmer renten og udsteder pengene.
sentence.en: The country's central bank sets the interest rate and issues the money.

en nationalitet.explanation: "En nationalitet" means "a nationality", which country you belong to. You can ask "Hvilken nationalitet har du?" (What nationality are you?) and answer "Jeg er dansk" (I am Danish).

sentence.da: Min mand har en anden **nationalitet** end mig.
sentence.en: My husband has a different nationality than me.
